text: Then he cried out in my hearing with a loud voice: "Draw near, you executioners of the city, each with his weapon of destruction in his hand!"

And behold, six men came from the direction of the upper gate, which faces north, each with his weapon for smashing in his hand; and among them was one man clothed in linen, with a writing case at his side. They came in and stood beside the bronze altar.

versions.text: And there came six men from the direction of the upper gate, which faces north, each with his weapon for slaughter in his hand; and among them was one man clothed in linen, with a writing case at his side. They came in and stood beside the bronze altar.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew מַפָּץ denotes a shattering or smashing instrument (a club or mace), not simply "slaughter." Rendering it as "smashing" also keeps it distinct from the different phrase in verse 1 (כְּלִי מַשְׁחֵתוֹ, "weapon of destruction").

versions.text: And there came six men from the direction of the upper gate, which faces north, each with his weapon for smashing in his hand; and among them was one man clothed in linen, with a writing case at his side. They came in and stood beside the bronze altar.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew opens with וְהִנֵּה, a presentational marker that heightens the vision's immediacy. Rendering it explicitly ("And behold") preserves the dramatic effect and gives the sentence a stronger opening beat for oral reading. The existing rendering absorbs the particle into "there came," which is defensible but flatter.

text: Now the glory of the God of Israel had risen from above the cherub where it had rested, and moved to the threshold of the temple. And he called to the man clothed in linen, who had the writing case at his side,
and the LORD said to him, "Pass through the city, through Jerusalem, and put a mark on the foreheads of those who sigh and groan over all the abominations committed within it."
And to the others he said in my hearing, "Pass through the city after him and strike. Show no pity; spare no one.

Slay them utterly—old men, young men and young women, children and women; but do not touch anyone who bears the mark. Begin at my sanctuary." So they began with the elders who were in front of the temple.

versions.text: Kill without mercy old men, young men and young women, children and women; but do not touch anyone who bears the mark. Begin at my sanctuary." So they began with the elders who were in front of the temple.
versions.explanation: לְמַשְׁחִית means "to destruction / utterly," not "without mercy"; the mercy language belongs to verse 5 ("show no pity"). Placing the verb first also restores the emphatic list of victims and improves the spoken rhythm.

text: Then he said to them, "Defile the temple and fill the courts with the slain. Go out!" So they went out and struck down people in the city.
While they were striking them down, I was left alone; and I fell on my face and cried out, "Ah, Lord GOD! Will you destroy the entire remnant of Israel as you pour out your wrath on Jerusalem?"

versions.text: While they were striking, and I was left alone, I fell on my face and cried out, "Ah, Lord GOD! Will you destroy the entire remnant of Israel as you pour out your wrath on Jerusalem?"
versions.explanation: The "While... and I was left alone, I fell" construction is ungrammatical and stumbles when read aloud. Separating the two clauses preserves the Hebrew sequence and reads smoothly.

versions.text: While they were striking, I was left alone; and I fell on my face and cried out, "Ah, Lord GOD! Will you destroy the entire remnant of Israel as you pour out your wrath on Jerusalem?"
versions.explanation: The Hebrew infinitive כְּהַכּוֹתָם carries an implied object (the people of the city, as in verse 7). "While they were striking" leaves the verb dangling without an object, which sounds incomplete when read aloud; "striking them down" matches the wording of verse 7 and completes the sense.

text: He said to me, "The guilt of the house of Israel and Judah is exceedingly great. The land is full of bloodshed and the city is full of injustice; for they say, 'The LORD has abandoned the land, and the LORD does not see.'
So I too will show no pity; I will not spare. I will bring down on their own heads what they have done."
And behold, the man clothed in linen, with the writing case at his side, brought back word: "I have done just as you commanded me."
